channel.title: Market Pressure Map · Indian markets
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Indian market sectors and the rupee, bonds, inflation and foreign flows.

item.title: Sensex soars 1,233 points to 75,692.78 and Nifty 1.68% to 23,440.80 as oil slides on Iran diplomacy
item.description:
Third straight gain; oil & gas and metal indices led while tech and media lagged. Nifty closed above its 50-day average. Builds on last week's recovery.

Why it matters: Falling crude and peace hopes cut India's biggest macro risk, lifting rate-sensitive and oil-consuming sectors and drawing foreign buyers back.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +2

Confidence: high · horizon: days

item.title: Brent plunges 7.63% to $104.77, its biggest drop in months, as Iran opens the door to talks
item.description:
WTI fell 7.36% to $96.46. Down from a six-month high of $117.64 on Friday. Reversing October's surge; strike risk after the 3 November US vote remains.

Why it matters: A $13 drop in three sessions sharply cuts India's import bill, fuel-subsidy risk and inflation pressure, easing the rupee and bond yields.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance +2, Inflation outlook +2

Confidence: high · horizon: days

item.title: Iran's supreme leader authorises the government to pursue peace talks with the US
item.description:
The US president says a deal 'could happen' and oil is 'dropping like a rock'. Iran still demands seven conditions and says Hormuz stays shut until the blockade ends. Biggest diplomatic step in weeks.

Why it matters: A path to reopening Hormuz would be the largest relief for India's oil, LNG and freight costs; conditions keep the outcome uncertain.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance +1, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: 10-year G-Sec yield falls nearly 10 basis points to about 7.32% as crude slides
item.description:
Down 17 bps from the 7.48% four-year high on 26 October; short covering added. Traders see 7.25% if oil keeps falling. Extending last week's easing.

Why it matters: Lower yields cut borrowing costs, lift bank bond portfolios and ease the government's financing burden.

Market gauges: Bond market (G-Secs) +2, Fiscal & trade balance +1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: Rupee slips 10 paise to 94.86 per dollar on a firm greenback despite the oil slide
item.description:
It touched 95.04 intraday. Traders see stabilisation after October's sharp gains. Pause, not reversal.

Why it matters: Cheaper oil should support the rupee in coming days; a firm dollar is limiting gains for now.

Market gauges: Rupee −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: Foreign investors buy a net ₹3,115 crore; domestic funds sell ₹392 crore (provisional)
item.description:
Second big buying day after ₹3,599 crore on Friday, following October's ₹52,100 crore outflow. Foreign funds still hold net short index futures. Reversing.

Why it matters: Returning foreign money supports large caps and the rupee; it depends on oil staying lower.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows +2

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: Major fire after a reported explosion at a state refinery in Visakhapatnam
item.description:
Flames and thick smoke near an oil tank; cause of the explosion is under scrutiny. New.

Why it matters: An outage at a coastal refinery could tighten local fuel supply and dent the refiner's output, though national impact depends on duration.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −1

Confidence: low · horizon: days

item.title: US conducts 'defensive strikes' on Iranian targets in Hormuz; Indian sailor killed off Oman
item.description:
Thirteen crew were rescued. A new wave of attacks hit tankers and an LNG carrier. Escalation on the water even as talks advance.

Why it matters: Continued attacks keep freight, insurance and crew risks high for Indian shipping and threaten the oil relief from diplomacy.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: India sources 70% of its crude imports from outside Hormuz, petroleum ministry says
item.description:
Diversification follows record imports of 5.6 million barrels a day. Ongoing shift away from Gulf routes.

Why it matters: Less reliance on Hormuz reduces supply-shock risk for Indian refiners, though longer routes raise freight costs.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: months
